A Rust project keeps application code in a Cargo package and development commands in a small Bun package.

## Generated files

```text
my-app/
├── resources/
│   └── icon.png
├── src/main.rs
├── Cargo.toml
├── Cargo.lock
├── quickgui.config.ts
├── package.json
└── README.md
```

Commit `Cargo.lock` after the first successful build. Split larger apps into ordinary Rust modules.

## Application entry

`src/main.rs` starts `Application::new().run(...)` and opens windows from that callback. Each window owns a `View`. `entry` in the config is the crate directory.

```rust
fn main() -> Result<(), quickgui::AppError> {
    Application::new().run(|cx| {
        cx.open_window(WindowOptions::new("My App").size(760.0, 520.0), App);
    })
}
```

## Configuration

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "@quickgui/cli";

export default defineConfig({
  language: "rust",
  name: "My App",
  identifier: "com.example.my-app",
  entry: ".",
  fonts: ["assets/MyFont.ttf"],
});
```

The application icon comes from `resources/icon.png`. Extra files can be listed in `resources`. See [App Icon](/docs/rust/app-icon) and [Bundled Resources](/docs/rust/bundled-resources). TOML supports the same keys. The CLI reads `quickgui.toml` before `quickgui.config.ts`. Enable optional crate features in `Cargo.toml` instead of setting `extensions` in the app config.

## Packages

Applications depend on the `quickgui` crate. `@quickgui/cli` is a development dependency. Optional `terminal` and `updater` capabilities are Cargo features. Keep the crate version already in your project:

```toml
[dependencies]
quickgui = { version = "...", features = ["updater"] }
```

## Local development

```sh
quickgui check
quickgui test
quickgui fmt
quickgui dev
quickgui build
```

`dev` rebuilds on source changes.
